title: What Garland thinks of Jelly Roll Morton's playing
summary: Asked about Jelly Roll, Garland says only that he had a style of his own that others copied.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: Oh, I'll say, listen. -- So, Tootie, so then, we've got all the stuff on the tape, Ed Garland as a studio player, as a band leader and playing a wide variety of music. And that's important so people don't get the idea that you just did one thing in your career, and then that's certainly not true, now, looking in the jazz books about people talking about Jelly Roll Morton, it seems as though everyone didn't have a high opinion -- of him, least not as high as he had when he made those tapes years ago for the Library of Congress. What do you remember about Jelly Roll?
Well, how'd he play, do you remember
Plays, all right, he's style, style of his own.
Did he influence any other players, other people play like in that style?
Do -- well I tell you, Jelly Roll -- Jelly Roll don't play like nobody else, he got his own style.
-- is all I can tell you about Jelly.
They said that Jelly copped it from somebody that most of them copy from him.
Jelly often sounded like me like he was playing the piano, like an -- a whole band.
You know, sort of like Duke played the piano.
